purpose: The countable lists. Every entry here is finite and nameable, and every one is something a drawing can be checked against without measuring a distance. Proportions and measurements are deliberately absent -- they live in the prose, because a measured quantity was repeatedly misread in this project while a countable list was not.

body_parts.source: Hampton, Figure Drawing: Design and Invention, p10. 'It is important to be aware that you are describing the eight parts of the body.'

line_kinds.source: Hampton p10. 'In this drawing process, you will never use any other type of line.'

drawing_stages.source: Hampton p35: looking for the skeleton is 'the second stage ... a transitional stage in developing volume'. Bradley's book adds detail and colour on top; Ishiwatari's thirteen-step pipeline splits the same whole into four of line and seven of colour.

fold_types.source: Bradley, Drawing People: How to Portray the Clothed Figure, ch.13.

causes.pipe: fabric falls freely from a condensed area; semicylindrical or semiconical
causes.zigzag: the inside of a bend in tubular cloth buckles; the stiffer the fabric the more angular
causes.spiral: tubular cloth condensing around a tubular form; the softer the fabric the rounder

face_parameters.source: More How To Draw Manga vol.4, Mastering Bishoujo Characters, p11: twelve types given as six opposed pairs.
face_parameters.note: These say who the character is, not whether the drawing is accurate. The eye-to-mouth distance being short is what makes a face read as a child's.

face_parts_for_combination.source: Tezuka, How to Draw Manga, p40: a table of four parts by eight variants, combined.
face_parts_for_combination.note: A face is built by combining parts, not by measuring one.

value_layers.source: comic-inking, ch.V. Objects beside each other but on different planes must not share a value.
value_layers.diagnostic: squint: a flat grey blur means a black and a white are missing

contour_jobs.source: comic-inking, ch.IV. Depth rule: heavy contour on the foreground, medium on the middle ground, fine on the background.

items: cursive (heaviest at the middle of a stroke)
angular or terse (heaviest at the end)
dead-weight (bold contour with fine interior detail)
contour_styles.source: comic-inking, ch.IV. Weights of a kind must agree with each other -- thin lines all alike, heavy lines all alike.

light_source_rule.summary: heavy line weight on the dark side of an object, thin on the light side

hair_rule.light_hair: cursive and elegant lines, weight set by the primary light source
hair_rule.dark_hair: follow the white highlight patterns; the negative space defines the hair's shape

three_dimensions_device.summary: draw an imaginary sphere around the subject and use it as the pivot; the camera, the light and the point of view all sit on that sphere
three_dimensions_device.source: Imagine FX Presents Anatomy vol.2, p62 (Ron Lemen). 'The circle is really a sphere. Ellipses with the long axis passing through circles center point.'

process_rule.summary: a rough sketch is a formal step: loose lines first, expressing the movement and the outline of the story, then inking and cleaning up, with the detail given by the variation of the line
process_rule.source: Super Anime Show 3: A Quick Study Book of Manga Sketching, ch.1-2

items: do not measure slowly -- 'the downside to slowly measuring out the figure is that it stiffens the poses' (Hampton p10)
do not let a stable symmetrical pose stand -- 'the action has either not begun, or it has ended' (Hampton p26)
do not use right angles -- 'organic shapes do not contain right angles' (comic-inking ch.VI)
do not overuse cross-hatching -- 'excessive cross-hatching is not a sign of artistic skill' (comic-inking ch.VII)
do not draw only what is necessary to describe the gesture -- 'render only what is necessary' (Hampton p28)
